title: The Biscuit Castle Key
markdown:
By the sea that sang soft songs, there was a special castle. It was not made of stone. It was made of yummy crumbly biscuits. Golden towers went up, up, up to the blue sky. Near this castle lived a little seal pup named Saffy. Saffy had soft fur and a little black nose that wiggled with curiosity. She loved to splash and play. She watched the biscuit castle and wondered about the warm treats inside.

Every day, the sea sang gentle songs. Saffy chased little fish that swam by, their scales flashing like tiny lights. She barked happy barks, like little bells. She felt very happy in the blue water. Not far from Saffy, in the wiggly green sea grass, lived Tint the little mermaid. Tint’s tail was so pretty, with shiny green scales that sparkled like jewels. Her hair floated around her like soft moonlight. Tint loved the quiet treasures of the ocean. She especially loved shells that told secrets of faraway dreams. Every day, Tint hummed soft songs to the waves. She looked for shells with a very special shine.

Until one afternoon, a little worry came, like a feather floating in the air. The big gate to the biscuit castle was stuck. Saffy pushed it with her nose. It would not open. The little gold key that hung on a string was gone. A little frown came over Saffy’s happy face. Her wiggles slowed down. Tint swam closer. She felt curious. Where did the little key go?

Because of that, Saffy and Tint decided to look for the key together. Saffy searched the shore, looking at every little spot and every smooth stone. Tint swam gracefully. She looked in the green sea grass, gently moving the leaves. They kept looking and looking. But the little key was nowhere to be found, as if it had melted into the sea.

Because of that, they kept looking with calm hearts. Saffy walked over to a pile of smooth rocks that lay in the warm sun. She gently nudged one with her nose, as if to ask if it had seen the key. Tint looked under a shiny rock with her sharp mermaid eyes. But still, the key would not show itself. A sad sigh came from Tint.

Until finally, as the sun started to go down, painting the sky with soft pink and orange colours, Saffy and Tint sat together on the warm sand. They felt quiet and thoughtful. Saffy sniffed the air, trying to smell the lost key. Just then, Saffy looked at the soft green leaves of the moon-kelp. A starfish was resting there, dreaming a deep sleepy dream. Saffy was very kind. She gave the sleepy starfish a gentle nudge with her nose. The starfish moved. Its tiny leg reached out, like it was waving hello. It pointed a little towards the moon-kelp. And there, nestled amongst the soft green leaves, shining with a soft warm light, was the little gold key.

Saffy gently picked up the little gold key in her soft mouth. Tint swam beside her, humming a happy song. Her green tail shimmered with joy. Together, they took the precious key back to the biscuit castle. With a soft happy little click, the gate swung open wide. A wonderful warm yummy smell of fresh biscuits filled the air. They shared the warm biscuits. Each bite tasted like sunshine and friendship.

Ever since that day, Saffy curled up on a soft sandy spot after play, and Tint snuggled down in her favourite seashell, and the biscuit castle key hung safe on its string, found again because two friends had looked closely, even in the quietest green leaves.
characters: Saffy (a seal pup), Tint (the tiny mermaid)
author: StoryGen Community
